section_summary.extract_value: This abstract reports one study using an online sample of 1,148 U.K. adults who completed multiple measures of positive body image and multidimensional well-being. After controlling for age and BMI, body appreciation predicted all well-being dimensions; other positive body-image measures predicted outcomes with mixed patterns by sex, and BMI was negatively associated with all body image measures.
section_summary.evidence_source: Studies examining associations between positive body image and wellbeing have used a limited array of measures of each construct. To rectify this, we asked an online sample of 1148 U.K. adults to complete a range of measures of positive body image (body appreciation, body image flexibility, body pride, body acceptance from others) and a multi-dimensional measure of well-being (emotional, psychological, and social).
